claim: Brodetto alla senigalliese is the local signature fish stew made with 13 types of fish (mantis shrimp, mullet, gurnard, sole, cuttlefish, monkfish, etc.) cooked slowly without stirring in tomato, vinegar and Verdicchio, served with garlic toast.
quote: The authentic recipe calls for 13 different types of fish... combined in a sauce of cherry tomatoes, peeled tomatoes, olive oil, onion, garlic, vinegar, and Verdicchio wine... served very hot with slices of toasted bread with garlic.

claim: Another typical Senigallia seafood dish is clams alla poveraccia, local clams cooked with garlic, anchovies, parsley and rosemary, served as antipasto or with spaghetti.
quote: clams alla poveraccia... features local clams cooked with garlic, anchovies in oil, parsley, and rosemary, served either as an appetizer or paired with spaghetti as a first course.

claim: Beyond the two starred restaurants, casual Senigallia options include Vicoletto da Michele, La Tartana, Da Carlo and Al Cuoco di Bordo, and a full fish dinner (fried olives, brodetto or passatelli, fish, dessert) typically costs 28-42 euros.
quote: famous restaurants ULIASSI and MADONNINA DEL PESCATORE... along with many others both by the sea and inland including Vicoletto da Michele, La Tartana, Da Carlo, and Al Cuoco di Bordo... A complete dinner... costs between 28 and 42 euros.

claim: The Foro Annonario is a neoclassical 1834 market (architect Pietro Ghinelli) of 24 Doric columns in the historic centre that houses a fish market on marble tables plus fruit/vegetable traders, and turns into a nightlife hub of bistros and pubs in the evening.
quote: designed by architect Pietro Ghinelli in 1834... circular shape adorned with 24 columns in Doric style... fish was bought and sold under the portico... In the evening the Foro Annonario with its clubs, bistros, pubs and restaurants becomes one of the places of nightlife.

claim: Gelateria Paolo Brunelli is Senigallia's celebrated gelato maker, ranked among Italy's best, with signature flavors like Crema Brunelli (cream, caramelized hazelnut, chocolate, Madagascar vanilla) and Portonovo (bitter Campari jelly).
quote: Paolo Brunelli... among the absolute best in the gelato world... signature Crema Brunelli, which combines cream, caramelized hazelnuts, chocolate, and vanilla from Madagascar. Other notable flavors are Portonovo, featuring bitter Campari jelly.

claim: Other recommended Senigallia gelaterias beyond Brunelli include Puro & Bio (unusual combos like melon and lavender) and Gelateria Papaya 2.0 (generous portions).
quote: Puro & Bio, which offers an impressive array of unique flavors with standout combinations like melon and lavender, and Gelateria Papaya 2.0, which offers a delightful array of flavors with generous portions.

claim: For aperitivo and wine, Senigallia's pedestrian centre offers wine bars including Saltatappo Vinoteca (strong local selection, good value), Galli Enoteca (historic-centre wine shop running tastings and winery tours) and Saffi Caffe (natural wines).
quote: Saltatappo Vinoteca - A charming wine bar in the heart of Senigallia... Galli Enoteca... reference point for all wine lovers... organises evenings, tastings and winery tours... Saffi Caffe... selection of natural wines.

claim: Vincisgrassi, a rich layered egg-pasta bake (ancestor of lasagna) with mixed-meat and chicken-giblet ragu and bechamel, is a must inland Marche pasta found on Senigallia tables.
quote: Vincisgrassi is one of the symbolic dishes of the Marchigian hinterland... egg pasta rolled out thinly and arranged in layers, alternated with a flavorful and full-bodied ragu, often prepared with mixed meat and chicken giblets... All the tables of the inhabitants of Senigallia... are absolutely laid with... renowned vincisgrassi.

claim: Marche street-food staples to try include olive all'ascolana (hand-pitted Ascolana olives stuffed with mixed meat, breaded and fried) and crescia sfogliata, a lard-rich rolled flatbread from the Pesaro-Urbino area.
quote: Olive ascolane... pitted by hand and stuffed with a mixed meat filling... breaded and fried... a true icon of Marchigian street food... Crescia sfogliata is a typical specialty of the provinces of Pesaro and Urbino... emblem of local street food.

claim: Moscioli are wild mussels growing naturally on the rocks between Ancona and Sirolo on the nearby Conero Riviera, a Slow Food Presidium since 2004, celebrated at the June 'Mosciolando' festival in Portonovo.
quote: The Portonovo Wild Mussel is a Slow Food presidium since 2004. Moscioli are wild mussels growing naturally in the stretch of sea between Pietralacroce (Ancona) and Sirolo... A festival dedicated to this specialty, Mosciolando, takes place in Portonovo in June.

claim: As of the 2025 season Slow Food Italia suspended the moscioli Presidium and asked the Ministry of Agriculture to block fishing of the species because the wild-mussel population is in steep decline, so visitors may not find authentic Portonovo moscioli.
quote: Slow Food Italia has officially suspended the Presidio and has submitted a request to the Ministry of Agriculture to block fishing of this species for the entire 2025 season. The mosciolo population is in constant decline.

claim: Highly rated casual seafood spots in Senigallia per diner reviews include Bruna Bistro, La Lampara and Il Mare in Terrazza, serving fritto misto, grilled sardoncini, shellfish and brodetto alla marchigiana with local Verdicchio.
quote: top-rated fish and seafood restaurants include Bruna Bistro, La Lampara, and Il Mare in Terrazza... Typical dishes include sardoncini scottadito (grilled sardines), fried fish, brodetto, mussels, clams, and sea snails.
